Hp.definition: ISA altitude corresponding to the local static pressure. Positive: pressure below ISA sea-level pressure.
Hp.limits: Pressure-altitude model: −5 to 84.852 km geopotential. Geometric altitude is converted before the atmosphere calculation.

Hg.definition: Geometric height above mean sea level. Positive: above mean sea level.
Hg.limits: Pressure-altitude model: −5 to 84.852 km geopotential. Geometric altitude is converted before the atmosphere calculation.

P.definition: Absolute static pressure of the surrounding air, related to density and absolute temperature by the ideal gas law.
P.limits: Pressure-altitude model: −5 to 84.852 km geopotential. Geometric altitude is converted before the atmosphere calculation.

Δ ISA.definition: Difference between actual static air temperature and ISA temperature at the same pressure altitude. Positive: warmer than ISA.

OAT.definition: Static temperature of the surrounding air.

TAS.definition: Magnitude of aircraft velocity relative to the surrounding air. Nonnegative.

CAS.definition: Airspeed at ISA sea-level conditions producing the same impact pressure as the actual flight condition, using the subsonic isentropic Pitot relation. Nonnegative.

EAS.definition: Airspeed at ISA sea-level conditions producing the same dynamic pressure as the actual flight condition. Nonnegative.

Mach.definition: Ratio of true airspeed to local speed of sound. Nonnegative.
Mach.limits: 0 ≤ M < 1 for the current compressibility model.

CL.definition: Aerodynamic lift divided by the product of dynamic pressure and wing reference area. Positive: lift toward the aircraft upper side.

Vs Factor.definition: Input multiplier applied to reference 1-g stall speed in CAS, with an optional additive CAS increment specified in knots. Nonnegative multiplier.

Ground Speed.definition: Magnitude of aircraft horizontal velocity relative to the ground. Nonnegative.

Qdyn.definition: Kinetic energy per unit volume of the air-relative flow. Nonnegative.

Qc.definition: Difference between stagnation pressure and static pressure. Nonnegative in the adopted subsonic model.

Weight.definition: Aircraft weight, expressed as mass in the selected units for aerodynamic calculations. Nonnegative.

Sref.definition: Wing reference area used to define aerodynamic coefficients. Positive area.

cref.definition: Wing reference chord used to calculate Reynolds number. Positive length.

CLmax.definition: Maximum lift coefficient attainable at the onset of stall for the selected aircraft configuration. Positive coefficient.

NzPullup.definition: Ratio of aerodynamic lift to aircraft weight in an unbanked maneuver. Positive: lift toward the aircraft upper side.

NzTurn.definition: Load factor in a coordinated level turn. Positive and not less than 1 in the adopted model.

BankTurn.definition: Aircraft bank angle in a coordinated level turn. Positive: right wing down.

Track.definition: Direction of the aircraft horizontal ground-velocity vector, measured clockwise from true north. Positive: clockwise (ground-velocity vector to the right).

Heading.definition: Direction in which the aircraft nose points, measured clockwise from true north. Positive: clockwise (nose to the right).

Sideslip.definition: Angle between the aircraft longitudinal axis and the incoming relative wind. Positive: relative wind coming from the right.

Drift.definition: Angular difference between heading and ground track (heading minus track). Positive: heading to the right of track.

HeadWind.definition: Wind component along the selected runway/reference direction. Positive: wind from ahead. Negative: tailwind.

Wind Speed.definition: Magnitude of horizontal wind velocity. Nonnegative.

CrossWind.definition: Wind component perpendicular to the selected runway/reference direction. Positive: wind coming from the right. Negative: wind from the left.

Runway Angle.definition: Direction of the selected runway/reference axis, measured clockwise from true north. Positive: clockwise (reference direction to the right).

Wind Direction.definition: Direction from which the wind blows, measured clockwise from true north. Positive: clockwise (wind-from direction to the right).

mass.MTOW.definition: Maximum takeoff weight approved for the aircraft, expressed as mass in the selected units.
mass.MTOW.use: Reference mass for takeoff-condition calculations when selected.

mass.MLW.definition: Maximum landing weight approved for the aircraft, expressed as mass in the selected units.
mass.MLW.use: Reference mass for landing-condition calculations when selected.

mass.MZFW.definition: Maximum zero-fuel weight, excluding usable fuel, expressed as mass in the selected units.
mass.MZFW.use: Reference mass for zero-fuel-mass calculations when selected.

mass.BOW.definition: Basic Operating Weight as defined by the aircraft manufacturer, expressed as mass in the selected units.
mass.BOW.use: Stored reference mass for calculations that use the selected aircraft mass.

mass.Heavy.definition: User-defined heavy reference weight, expressed as mass in the selected units. Not a certified weight limit.
mass.Heavy.use: User-defined reference mass for calculations that use the selected aircraft mass.

mass.Light.definition: User-defined light reference weight, expressed as mass in the selected units. Not a certified weight limit.
mass.Light.use: User-defined reference mass for calculations that use the selected aircraft mass.

CLmaxFlap.full: Maximum lift coefficient by flap setting
CLmaxFlap.definition: Maximum lift coefficient for the specified flap configuration, supplied from aircraft aerodynamic data. Positive coefficient.
CLmaxFlap.use: Used with mass, density, and reference area to calculate reference stall speed.

Pressure Altitude.definition: ISA altitude corresponding to the local static pressure. Positive: pressure below ISA sea-level pressure.
Pressure Altitude.limits: Pressure-altitude model: −5 to 84.852 km geopotential. See the documented geometric-altitude temperature convention.

Geometric Altitude.definition: Geometric height above mean sea level. Positive: above mean sea level.
Geometric Altitude.limits: Pressure-altitude model: −5 to 84.852 km geopotential. See the documented geometric-altitude temperature convention.

Pressure.definition: Absolute static pressure of the surrounding air, related to density and absolute temperature by the ideal gas law.

Temperature.definition: Static temperature of the surrounding air.

Delta ISA.definition: Difference between actual static air temperature and ISA temperature at the same pressure altitude. Positive: warmer than ISA.

True Airspeed.definition: Magnitude of aircraft velocity relative to the surrounding air. Nonnegative.

Calibrated Airspeed.definition: Airspeed at ISA sea-level conditions producing the same impact pressure as the actual flight condition, using the subsonic isentropic Pitot relation. Nonnegative.

Equivalent Airspeed.definition: Airspeed at ISA sea-level conditions producing the same dynamic pressure as the actual flight condition. Nonnegative.

Lift Coefficient CL.definition: Aerodynamic lift divided by the product of dynamic pressure and wing reference area. Positive: lift toward the aircraft upper side.
Lift Coefficient CL.limits: Available when dynamic pressure and reference area are positive. The sign follows the selected load factor.

Dynamic Pressure.definition: Kinetic energy per unit volume of the air-relative flow. Nonnegative.

Impact Pressure.definition: Difference between stagnation pressure and static pressure. Nonnegative in the adopted subsonic model.

Bank Angle φ.definition: Aircraft bank angle in a coordinated level turn. Positive: right wing down.

Track Angle.definition: Direction of the aircraft horizontal ground-velocity vector, measured clockwise from true north. Positive: clockwise (ground-velocity vector to the right).

Heading Angle Ψ.definition: Direction in which the aircraft nose points, measured clockwise from true north. Positive: clockwise (nose to the right).

Drift Angle.definition: Angular difference between heading and ground track (heading minus track). Positive: heading to the right of track.

Sideslip Angle β.definition: Angle between the aircraft longitudinal axis and the incoming relative wind. Positive: relative wind coming from the right.

Ground Speed.definition: Magnitude of aircraft horizontal velocity relative to the ground. Nonnegative.

Vs Factor.definition: Ratio of current calibrated airspeed to reference 1-g stall speed in CAS. Nonnegative.

Mach.definition: Ratio of true airspeed to local speed of sound. Nonnegative.
Mach.limits: 0 ≤ M < 1 for the current compressibility model.

Wind Speed.definition: Magnitude of horizontal wind velocity. Nonnegative.

Wind Direction.definition: Direction from which the wind blows, measured clockwise from true north. Positive: clockwise (wind-from direction to the right).

Geopotential Altitude.definition: Altitude equivalent to gravitational potential energy per unit mass under constant standard gravity. Positive: above the reference datum.
Geopotential Altitude.equation: H = r h / (r + h); for Hp/P input, H = Hp − 29.271247 ΔT ln(p/p0)
Geopotential Altitude.limits: Pressure-altitude model: −5 to 84.852 km geopotential. See the documented geometric-altitude temperature convention.

Density Altitude.definition: ISA altitude corresponding to the actual air density. Positive: above ISA sea level.

Temperature Altitude.definition: Tropospheric ISA altitude corresponding to actual static temperature, limited to 11 km in this model. Positive: above ISA sea level.

Density.definition: Mass of air per unit volume, calculated from static pressure and absolute temperature using the ideal gas law. Positive scalar.

Total Temperature.definition: Ideal stagnation temperature obtained by adiabatically bringing the air-relative flow to rest, without probe recovery corrections.

Viscosity.definition: Dynamic viscosity of air relates shear stress to velocity gradient; its temperature dependence is modeled by Sutherland's law. Positive scalar.

Sound Speed.definition: Speed of propagation of small pressure disturbances in the surrounding air. Positive scalar.

Stall Speed Vs.definition: Reference 1-g calibrated airspeed at which the required lift coefficient equals CLmax for the selected aircraft mass and configuration. Nonnegative.
Stall Speed Vs.equation: Vs,TAS = √(2 m g0 / (ρ S CLmax)); displayed Vs,CAS = CAS(Vs,TAS)

Reynolds.definition: Ratio of inertial to viscous effects based on true airspeed and reference chord. Nonnegative.

Pressure Ratio δ.definition: Ratio of local static pressure to standard sea-level pressure. Positive scalar.

Density Ratio σ.definition: Ratio of local air density to standard sea-level density. Positive scalar.

Temperature Ratio θ.definition: Ratio of local absolute temperature to standard sea-level absolute temperature. Positive scalar.

Total Pressure.definition: Stagnation pressure of the air-relative flow under isentropic conditions.

DynPressure * S / g.definition: Aerodynamic reference force qS for a unit lift coefficient (CL = 1), expressed in kilogram-force (kgf). Nonnegative.

Lift Force.definition: Aerodynamic lift force required by the selected load factor. Positive: lift toward the aircraft upper side.
Lift Force.equation: L / g0 = q S CL / g0 (displayed as kgf)

Weight/Delta W/δ.definition: Aircraft weight divided by atmospheric pressure ratio δ, expressed in kilogram-force (kgf). Positive for positive aircraft weight.

Load Factor Nz.definition: Ratio of aerodynamic lift to aircraft weight. Positive: lift toward the aircraft upper side.

Turn Radius.definition: Signed radius of a coordinated level turn relative to the air mass. Positive: right turn. Negative: left turn.

Turn Rate.definition: Rate of change of aircraft heading in a coordinated level turn. Positive: clockwise (right turn).

AlongTrack Headwind.definition: Wind component along the aircraft ground track. Positive: wind from ahead. Negative: tailwind.

AlongTrack Crosswind.definition: Wind component perpendicular to the aircraft ground track. Positive: wind coming from the right. Negative: wind from the left.
